conviction_note: Two sides that roughly offset. Upside: the stock is down 17% in 20 days and sits 3% above its 52-week low while retail ETFs are near highs. The street's FY EPS ($2.33) is below the company's own guide floor ($2.35). The Section 301 rate appears to have stayed at 10%, which management said would add about $35M to the year. And this name has paid +8% and +13% for its last two EPS beat-and-raise prints. Downside: Old Navy laps a +6% comp, card data shows clothing spend fell to +1% YoY in October, management said in August that trend supported only the low end of the Q3 sales guide, and TJX blamed warm weather for a slow November. p_up of 54 against abs 12.5 gives +1.0. The findings sum to +0.6. The two agree in sign and both are small, because the positive lean agrees with the call-bid skew and is partly priced.

next_guide.basis: The EPS and margin guide is likely held or raised: management flagged about $35M of further benefit if the 10% Section 301 rate held through Q3, and no rate increase was found. The FY sales guide risks being trimmed to the low end: August trend supported the low end of Q3, October clothing card spend slowed to +1%, TJX blamed warm weather for a slow November, and a new Old Navy CEO started Nov 2. Net: EPS maintained or raised, sales maintained or narrowed lower.

findings.finding: GAP fell 17.2% in 20 sessions and 10.75% in 5 into the print and sits 3.35% above its 52-week low. Over the same weeks the retail sector ETF (XRT) stayed near its high, NAV $90.66 on Nov 12 against a 52-week high of 93.52. Spot about $19 is 28% below the $26.26 mean target. No company-specific cause was found for the slide. The two prints that showed an EPS beat and a margin/EPS raise paid +8.2% and +12.9%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 (2026-08-27): stock had drifted lower into the print, then EPS beat with a raised EPS guide and Old Navy -4%, +12.94%. Q3 FY25: +8.24% on beat and raise. Two Old Navy-driven sales-guide cuts: -14.41% and -15.40%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a statement about what is priced, not about what is unpriced: the bar has fallen. If the slide reflected known bad news, there would be a downgrade, a pre-release or an 8-K. None was found (EDGAR shows only Forms 3/4/144, 13D/A and a board appointment since Sep 15). Calls are bid (skew -13.2), so options partly carry this upside already. Sized below the reaction to the last beat-and-raise for that reason.
findings.independence: Sector comparison: https://www.ssga.com/us/en/individual/etfs/state-street-spdr-sp-retail-etf-xrt. Simply Wall St 2026-11-18 also finds no single cause: https://sg.finance.yahoo.com/news/gap-gap-shares-dropped-driving-081336220.html

findings.finding: Street FY26 adjusted EPS of $2.33 sits below the company's own raised guide floor of $2.35 (range $2.35-2.45). Q3 consensus EPS of $0.73 matches only the low end of what the Q3 guide implies (sales +1.5-2.5%, GM +25-75bp on 42.4%, slight SG&A leverage on 33.9% give roughly $0.73-0.79 at ~365M shares and 25.5% tax). The street is haircutting management on EPS. The Q2 profit beat came with management saying it 'exceeded our profit expectations'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 EPS beat $0.52 against $0.50 plus a raise: +12.94%. Q1 FY26 slight EPS miss plus a sales cut: -15.40%.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus is visible, but a street sitting under the guide floor means an in-guide print is an EPS beat. If priced, the whisper would sit above the guide midpoint rather than at $0.75. Capped small because the EPS consensus has one source.
findings.independence: Guide arithmetic from the company 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000039911/000162828026059262/q22026eprexhibit991.htm. Same EW article as the revenue bar.

findings.finding: On the Aug 27 call the CFO said, of the Q3 sales guide of +1.5% to +2.5%, that 'our current trend supports the low end of our outlook'. On a $3.9B base the low end is about $3.96-4.00B. The street's $4.02B sits at the guide midpoint, above management's own read of trend.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue misses have coincided with large moves both ways depending on margin. Q2 FY26 revenue missed ($3.65B against $3.72B) and the stock rose 12.9% on EPS and guide. Q1 FY26 revenue miss with a sales-guide cut: -15.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: A consensus at $4.02B, above the trend-supported low end, shows the street did not anchor on the caveat. Stock reactions on this name have followed EPS and guide more than revenue, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: October clothing card spend slowed (BofA Institute, separate finding). Same call script as the Old Navy compare finding.

findings.finding: Old Navy laps a +6% Q3 FY25 comp, against +2% in Q2 FY25. Q2 FY26 ran -4% on a +2% compare, a two-year stack of -2. The Q3 guide of flat to -1% needs a two-year stack of +5 to +6, a 7-8 point acceleration. Old Navy is about 56% of sales ($2.06B of $3.65B in Q2). Net of the rest: Gap brand (~23%, +10% comp, lapping +7%) and BR (+3%) would have to stay strong, and Athleta (-12%) laps a weak compare.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Old Navy comp is the line the stock trades on. Misses led to -14.41% (Mar 2026) and -15.40% (May 2026). The Q2 -4% (worse than guide) was overridden by EPS and guide: +12.94%.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews quote the flat to -1% guide and the -4% Q2 figure, but none found quotes the +6% compare. Management said in August that Q3-to-date trends were 'in line with the range'. That covers August only and lands inside the guide, which shrinks this finding.
findings.independence: Q3 FY25 Old Navy +6% comp per Gap's Q3 FY25 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/39911/000162828025053392/q32025eprexhibit991.htm). Shares the Q2 8-K with other findings.

findings.finding: Bank of America card data (published Nov 12): clothing spend per household grew about +3.9% YoY in August, +3.6% in September and +1.0% in October, cooling more than other categories. Census October retail sales (Nov 17) also showed clothing stores declining, -0.7% m/m per a secondary report. Gap's Q3 is August to October, so the last month of its quarter was the weakest.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history of this stock reacting to card data. The line it feeds is Old Navy comp and revenue (see above).
findings.why_not_priced: Public macro proxy: part of the pre-print slide may be this. Industry card spend averaged about +2.8% over the quarter, roughly in line with a +1.5-2.5% sales guide, so it argues for the low end rather than a miss. It is a proxy and not company-level, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Census October retail: https://www.wcax.com/2026/11/17/spending-growth-slowed-retail-stores-october-high-prices-give-shoppers-pause/ (clothing stores among the declines). BofA's own holiday-items cut shows clothing +8.7% in October, so the series is mixed.

findings.finding: TJX (Nov 18, same Aug-Oct quarter) posted a Marmaxx comp of +2% against about +1% expected, with apparel and home improving from Q2 (+1%). TJX rose 8-10%. It reads as an improving Q3 for value apparel. Link: TJX/Marmaxx is the largest off-price apparel competitor for the same value-apparel customer Old Navy serves, over the same August-October quarter. No revenue tie.
findings.link: Same product (value apparel), same customer, same quarter (TJX Q3 ended Oct 31, Gap Q3 ended ~Nov 1); competitor, not counterparty; no shared-revenue figure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GAP closed +2.5% on Nov 18, the day TJX reported.
findings.why_not_priced: GAP already rose 2.5% on the day, so this is partly priced. Off-price gaining traffic can also be share taken from Old Navy, so the sign for Gap is ambiguous and the size small.
findings.independence: TJX 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000109198/000010919826000058/tjxq3fy27earningspressrele.htm. Shares this document with the warm-weather finding.

findings.finding: TJX management blamed 'unseasonably warm weather in the U.S. and Canada' for a slow start to Q4 (November) and would not say whether quarter-to-date sales were positive. Gap will give quarter-to-date and holiday commentary on Nov 19 for a Q4 that includes November, and its Q4 and FY sales view is exposed to the same weather.
findings.link: Same calendar weeks (Nov 2026), same North American apparel demand; competitor.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sales-guide cuts drove -14.4% and -15.4%. FY sales was trimmed in Aug yet the stock rose on the EPS raise.
findings.why_not_priced: Public from Nov 18, and GAP fell 4% on Nov 19 intraday, so it is partly in. A weather read has not paid on its own in this repo's record, so sized small.
findings.independence: TJX release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000109198/000010919826000058/tjxq3fy27earningspressrele.htm (same company, one document family as the peer finding).

findings.finding: On Aug 27 Gap said that if the 10% Section 301 rate held through the end of Q3 it would add about $35M of benefit to the year, beyond the $15M already in the guide. The USTR notice of 2026-07-28 set the rates at 10%/12.5% from Jul 24, and no increase through October was found. $35M after tax is about $0.07 per share on 367M shares. That supports holding or raising the $2.35-2.45 EPS guide, against a street at $2.33.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS/margin guide raises: +12.94% (Aug 2026, raised to $2.35-2.45) and +8.24% (Nov 2025, operating-margin raise).
findings.why_not_priced: If priced, the street FY EPS would sit at or above the $2.40 midpoint. It sits at $2.33, below the floor. Management may instead spend the relief on Old Navy price investment (they did so with half the Section 122 relief), which caps this finding.
findings.independence: Federal Register notice of Section 301 actions: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/28/2026-15181/notice-of-actions-in-section-301-investigations-of-acts-policies-and-practices-of-various-economies

findings.finding: The remaining IEEPA refunds (about $417M of $512M, plus interest) were expected to arrive in Q3. Gap had $2.5B of cash, $399M left on its buyback authorization after $601M bought YTD, and FY share count guided at 367M. A new authorization or an accelerated repurchase alongside the print is plausible. The refund itself is excluded from adjusted EPS (a one-off); the path to the multiple is capital return.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 included a $200M ASR completion plus $200M open-market buying. That print rose 12.9%, but on EPS and guide, not attributable to the buyback.
findings.why_not_priced: No new authorization has been announced. A board approval would be visible as an 8-K or in the release. Speculative, so small.
findings.independence: The Q2 call script confirms about $400M remaining and the capital framework: https://s204.q4cdn.com/320226404/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Gap-Inc-Q2-2026-Earnings-Conference-Call-Script.pdf

findings.finding: Michael Francis became President and CEO of Old Navy on Nov 2, 2026, the day after Q3 closed. A new brand CEO's first public outlook carries a risk of a reset to holiday and Q4 Old Navy expectations.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not observed on this name; Old Navy outlook cuts drove -14% and -15%.
findings.why_not_priced: Known since August. Francis helped build the H2 plan (call script), which weakens the reset case. Kept small.
findings.independence: Call script: Francis 'worked closely together to develop our plans for the second half', which cuts against a reset.

findings.finding: Director and 10% owner William S. Fisher sold 433,656 shares at $23.35 on Oct 5 and 500,000 at $23.89 on Oct 6, not under a 10b5-1 plan. A 13D/A followed Oct 8. The Fisher family has filed a string of 13D/A amendments through Aug-Oct, a routine selling pattern.

baseline_tension: The positive lean agrees with the call-bid skew (-13.2) and cuts against the -17% run-up only in the sense that the run-up lowered the bar. Because it agrees with the skew it is partly priced, so p_up is held at 54 rather than higher. The negatives (Old Navy compare, October slowdown, warm November) are probably part of why the stock already fell.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 / core skew row: the run-up/expectations finding agrees with a call-bid skew, so it was cut from +2.0 to +1.5 and p_up from 55 to 54.
Lesson 6: the EPS consensus ($0.73, $2.33) has one source, so the street-below-guide finding was capped from +1.5 to +1.0.
Lesson 5: proxies shrunk. BofA/Census clothing -1.0 to -0.7; TJX warm-weather Q4 read -1.0 to -0.7; gas/macro -0.3 to -0.2.
Lesson 9: Old Navy compare finding sized net of Gap brand (+10%) and BR. -1.5 to -1.2.
Lesson 2: tariff refund treated as a one-off, sized only through a capital-return path. +0.5 to +0.4.

Two zero-size items (analyst PT moves, Nov 10 dividend timing) were added after reading as completeness filings and change nothing; print_vs_bar moved from -0.5 to -0.3 after re-reading that the guide low end is about $3.96-4.00B.
Left standing: tariff-301 next-guide finding (+1.5, document-based, on the line this name has paid for), revenue-low-end statement (-1.0), new Old Navy CEO reset risk (-0.5).
